channel.title: The Git Reporter
channel.description: A code-native newspaper of meaningful software change.

item.title: Qwen Code Saves the Shape of a Finished Workflow
item.description: Qwen Code is teaching a finished multi-agent run to leave behind a reviewable shape—rather than a pile of logs that dies with the terminal.

item.title: Cline Lets an Agent Schedule Work—But Not Anywhere It Likes
item.description: Cline's new durable task system lets an agent make work recur after the chat ends, but its public implementation keeps asking the harder question: which workspace gave that job authority?

item.title: Pi's New Harness Writes the Restart Point Before It Acts
item.description: Pi's dev branch is turning an agent run into a durable, remotely attachable session—but its most important promise is also the simplest: record the restart point before the model or tool gets to act.

item.title: An Approval Must Keep Its Denials
item.description: Codex is tightening the rules beneath its approval layer: a broad remembered grant must not reopen a denied child path, an unfamiliar shell must identify itself, and a stale reviewer score should be visible as stale.

item.title: An Agent Can’t Review the Wrong Tree
item.description: Qwen Code has made a workflow subagent’s linked worktree part of the job itself—a small API change with a large warning for anyone resuming, reviewing, or testing code across branches.

item.title: API Discovery: Cloudflare’s Gateway Keeps Native Agent APIs Intact
item.description: Cloudflare’s public Responses and Messages endpoints give agent builders a choice that generic gateway adapters often erase: keep the provider-shaped request format that the workflow actually needs.

item.title: Builder Work: Hermes Keeps an SDK Upgrade From Dropping the Conversation
item.description: A public Claude-assisted MCP migration in Hermes Agent shows the durable craft: make a compatibility seam explicit, then test every way an upgrade can lose meaning without crashing.

item.title: When a Context Limit Drops the User’s Turn
item.description: OpenClaw found a required Codex compaction preflight treating an intentional no-op as a fatal failure—so an overlong session could lose the incoming user turn before the model ever answered.

item.title: API Discovery: Pi’s xAI Route Keeps Reasoning State in Play
item.description: Pi now sends every built-in xAI model through the Responses API—a useful route for agents that need a deliberate, client-owned continuity plan rather than a model-name swap.

item.title: Builder Work: A Test Double Is a Contract
item.description: Unsloth’s agent-assisted CI repair shows a durable testing move: put a shared fake at the same interface boundary as production, then make the test harness reveal the task that actually failed.

item.title: A Sandbox Isn’t Finished Until the Repository Says So
item.description: Mastra Factory is making one understated agent-system choice explicit: before a session workspace is scrubbed, pooled, or destroyed, the repository can say how its own worktree should be put away.

item.title: Codex Stops a Thread’s Permission From Leaking Into a Read-Only Environment
item.description: A new Codex regression test makes the sharpest promise in its permissions work: a selected environment configured read-only must stay read-only even when the surrounding thread can write.

item.title: API Discovery: OpenWork’s MCP Apps Stay Inside the Server That Served Them
item.description: OpenWork’s public MCP Apps contract gives a small agent interface one useful rule: its UI resource and tool calls stay with the MCP server that supplied them.

item.title: A Forgotten Tool Is No Longer Callable in Pydantic AI
item.description: After compaction hides how a deferred tool reached an agent, Pydantic AI now makes the agent put that evidence back before the call can go through.

item.title: A Session Approval Needs Something to Hold On To
item.description: Two fresh code changes make the same point: a human’s “yes” is only useful when an agent can name exactly what that yes still authorizes.

item.title: API Discovery: Pydantic AI Maps the FastMCP 4 Fault Line
item.description: Pydantic AI’s public MCPToolset now bridges FastMCP 3 and 4—but the documented differences are the point of the upgrade plan.

item.title: CrewAI’s Flow Telemetry Learns Where a Run Actually Stopped
item.description: CrewAI’s public agent-assisted telemetry change teaches a durable craft: model a run’s lifecycle explicitly instead of guessing the ending from a start event.

item.title: OpenClaw’s shared channels gain a per-requester login
item.description: A new opt-in OAuth mode for HTTP MCP servers lets a trusted sender connect their own account instead of letting the whole room run on one operator credential.

item.title: API Discovery: Pi converts strict tool schemas at the provider boundary
item.description: Pi’s public constrained-sampling API now has a fresher compatibility layer for builders who want strict tool calls without permanently rewriting the schema their application owns.

item.title: Unsloth Desktop Turns the Local Model Into an Open-Harness Backend
item.description: The beta is more than a local-model GUI: it puts training, export, three compatibility APIs, harness-specific adapters, and a model-control plane on one machine—creating a serious test bench for separating the model from the agent that drives it.

item.title: Coding Agents Are Building Themselves—But Git Can Prove Only Part of It
item.description: Across 40,345 unique commits in ten public agent codebases, coding-agent credit becomes sharply more visible in 2026—and the missing receipts matter as much as the names that appear.

item.title: In Mastra’s Approval Queue, the Second Yes Needs Its Own Address
item.description: An open Mastra core pull request treats a human approval as a per-tool-call decision, not a vague signal attached to an entire agent run.

item.title: API Discovery: Let an ACP Session Reply Before You Light Up the Client
item.description: The Agent Client Protocol’s public TypeScript SDK gives a client a newSession() promise; a fresh Goose change shows why that reply is a useful readiness boundary.

item.title: Builder Work: Qwen Code Makes Workflow Advice Load-Bearing
item.description: Qwen Code’s newly merged workflow guidance teaches a transferable engineering move: make agent-facing policy executable enough to fail a regression test.

item.title: Cline gives a finished agent answer a diff receipt
item.description: Cline’s restored “View Changes” control makes a completed agent turn point to a checkpointed file delta—not just its own verdict.

item.title: Agent Plugins Standardizes the Box, Not What Runs Inside
item.description: Five client families now accept one Skills-and-MCP package. The first compatibility gap shows why the harder standard begins where this one stops.

item.title: API Discovery: Pydantic AI routes Cortex work through Snowflake
item.description: Pydantic AI now has a Snowflake Cortex provider, but a useful trial starts by checking the selected model’s capability boundary—not by assuming one adapter makes every model equivalent.

item.title: CrewAI teaches telemetry to separate the agent from the room
item.description: CrewAI’s agent-assisted telemetry change makes one reusable move: record who drove a process separately from where the process ran.

item.title: Hermes now stops agents from quietly rewriting their own instructions
item.description: A new Hermes Agent write gate treats project instruction files as a persistence surface: even an auto-approved agent must ask a human before it changes the text that can steer tomorrow’s work.

item.title: OpenWork learns to wait for a turn that has actually started
item.description: OpenWork’s new headless-thread client turns a subtle race into an explicit contract: an agent turn is not finished just because its status looks idle.
